mainTopic: Blessings that ceased: the אורים ותומים, prophecy, the שמיר, נופת צופים and אנשי אמנה
overview: The עמוד asks who the 'early prophets' in the משנה are, since the אורים ותומים stopped when they died. רב הונא says they are דוד, שמואל and שלמה. A ברייתא shows that the אורים ותומים lasted until the first בית המקדש was destroyed. So רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that 'early' only excludes the last prophets, חגי, זכריה and מלאכי. After them רוח הקודש left ישראל, but a בת קול still spoke, pointing to הלל הזקן and later שמואל הקטן. Next the גמרא discusses the שמיר: רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה argue whether iron tools cut the stones of the בית המקדש, and the שמיר is shown engraving the stones of the חושן. The גמרא then lists more things lost with the first בית המקדש and explains נופת צופים and the word זיפים. Finally it explains 'אנשי אמנה' as people who trust הקב"ה and begins רבא's reading of 'יום קטנות', which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: End of the verse about שאול opening its mouth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting ישעיהו 5:14, the closing proof of the earlier discussion. The פסוק describes the netherworld swallowing people up.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The netherworld has opened wide its throat and gaped its mouth without limit, and down go her glory, her crowd, her noise, and whoever rejoices in her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a פסוק it started quoting just before this section. The פסוק is the proof for the punishment described in the earlier discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is argued here. This is the tail end of a source the גמרא already began quoting. Once it ends, the גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה.

phrases.english: The netherworld has opened wide its throat
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 5:14.

phrases.english: and gaped its mouth without limit,
and down go her glory and her crowd,
and her noise, and whoever rejoices in her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a verse begun in the previous discussion.
steps.raayaObject: The punishment described in the preceding discussion

steps.title: Who are 'the early prophets'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'from when the early prophets died' and asks who they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'From when the early prophets died' (the אורים ותומים stopped). Who are 'the early prophets'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line of the משנה and asks what 'the early prophets' means. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ties the end of the אורים ותומים to the death of 'the early prophets', but it doesn't say who they were. Knowing who they were tells us when the אורים ותומים stopped working.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן גדול's breastplate, used to ask ה׳ questions and get answers

phrases.english: "From when the early prophets died."
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. It continues: the אורים ותומים stopped.

phrases.english: Who are "the early prophets"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of 'the early prophets', which tells us when the אורים ותומים stopped

steps.title: רב הונא: דוד, שמואל and שלמה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the early prophets are דוד, שמואל and שלמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: These are דוד, שמואל and שלמה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. The early prophets are דוד, שמואל and שלמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב הונא, the אורים ותומים stopped answering after שלמה died. That is long before the first בית המקדש was destroyed, and this becomes important later in the section.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question

phrases.english: רב הונא said:
This means David, Samuel and Solomon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The early prophets are דוד, שמואל and שלמה, so the אורים ותומים stopped after שלמה.

steps.title: רב נחמן: even in דוד's days it didn't always answer
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that in דוד's days the אורים ותומים sometimes answered and sometimes didn't. He proves this from צדוק, who got an answer, and אביתר, who did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: In the days of דוד, sometimes an answer came up and sometimes it did not. צדוק asked and got an answer. אביתר asked and did not get one, as it says: 'And אביתר went up.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds a detail: even back in דוד's time, the אורים ותומים did not always answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof is that two כהנים asked in the same period, and only צדוק got an answer. The phrase 'and אביתר went up' is read as אביתר stepping away because he got no answer. This shows the answers were already unreliable in דוד's day.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן גדול in דוד's time
Another כהן גדול in דוד's time

phrases.english: רב נחמן said: In the days of David,
sometimes it came up, and sometimes it did not come up,
phrases.notes: 'It' means an answer from the אורים ותומים.

phrases.english: for Tzadok asked, and it came up for him,
Abiathar asked, and it did not come up for him,
as it says: "And Abiathar went up."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 15:24. 'Went up' is read as אביתר stepping away from serving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second view next to רב הונא's answer, describing how the אורים ותומים worked in דוד's time.

steps.title: רבה בר שמואל: a פסוק about seeking ה׳ in זכריהו's days
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל quotes a פסוק saying people sought ה׳ in the days of זכריהו, long after שלמה. He suggests this means through the אורים ותומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שמואל objected: 'He set himself to seek God in the days of זכריהו, who understood the visions of God.' Doesn't this mean through the אורים ותומים?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שמואל challenges רב הונא. He brings a פסוק which seems to show the אורים ותומים still worked after שלמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the אורים ותומים ended with שלמה, nobody could use it in the later days of זכריהו. Reading 'to seek God' as asking the אורים ותומים would contradict רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: To seek God (ask ה׳ for guidance)

phrases.english: Rabba bar Shmuel objected:
"And he set himself to seek God in the days of Zechariah,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 26:5. The פסוק is about King עזיהו.

phrases.english: who understood the visions of God."
Isn't it through the Urim VeTummim?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's claim that the אורים ותומים ended after שלמה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that the אורים ותומים ended with שלמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק describes seeking ה׳ in the time of זכריהו, after שלמה, which suggests the אורים ותומים still worked then.

steps.title: No, it means through prophets
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק means seeking ה׳ through prophets, not through the אורים ותומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means through prophets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the objection. 'Seeking God' in that פסוק means asking prophets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק never mentions the אורים ותומים, and זכריהו is described as someone who 'understood the visions of God', which fits prophecy. So the פסוק does not prove that the אורים ותומים worked after שלמה, and רב הונא's view stands.

phrases.english: No, through prophets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק describes asking the אורים ותומים after שלמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק describes asking prophets, so it does not challenge רב הונא.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the אורים ותומים ended with the first בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying that when the first בית המקדש was destroyed, the cities of the לויים, the אורים ותומים, and the kingship of the house of דוד all came to an end.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: From when the first בית המקדש was destroyed, the open-land cities stopped, the אורים ותומים ended, and the king from the house of דוד ended.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, about when the אורים ותומים ended. This sets up a new challenge to רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the אורים ותומים ended only when the first בית המקדש was destroyed. That is centuries after שלמה, which seems to contradict רב הונא's view that it ended with the early prophets.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source as proof)
The cities of the לויים with open land around them
A king from the family of דוד

phrases.english: Come and hear:
From when the First Temple was destroyed,
the cities with open land were cancelled,
phrases.notes: These are the cities given to the לויים, with fields around them.

phrases.english: and the Urim VeTummim stopped,
and the king from the house of David stopped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source about when the אורים ותומים ended, which seems to clash with רב הונא.
steps.raayaObject: The time when the אורים ותומים ended
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing what ended when the first בית המקדש was destroyed
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that the אורים ותומים ended with דוד, שמואל and שלמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא puts the end of the אורים ותומים at the destruction of the first בית המקדש, centuries after שלמה, so 'early prophets' cannot mean only דוד, שמואל and שלמה.

steps.title: The ברייתא explains away the פסוק in עזרא about the אורים ותומים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Someone might quote a פסוק in עזרא that sounds like the אורים ותומים would come back soon in the second בית המקדש. The ברייתא answers that the פסוק means 'until the far-off future,' like saying 'until משיח comes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if someone whispers to you, 'But the פסוק says they may not eat קדשי קדשים until a כהן stands with the אורים ותומים,' tell him: that is like a person telling his friend, 'until the dead come back to life and משיח בן דוד comes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step keeps going. It blocks a possible objection from a פסוק in עזרא, so its point stands: the אורים ותומים ended with the first בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could make it sound like the אורים ותומים were expected back any day in the second בית המקדש. The ברייתא says 'until' here means a far-future time, like the days of משיח. So the proof stays strong that the אורים ותומים lasted until the first בית המקדש was destroyed, long after שלמה. That is a problem for רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: whispers to you (raises a doubt with you)
the Tirshatha, a title for the leader in the days of עזרא
the most holy offerings, which only כהנים may eat

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק is not saying the אורים ותומים were about to return. The ברייתא reads 'until' as 'in the far-off future, at the time of משיח.'

phrases.english: And if a person whispers to you, saying:
"And the Tirshatha said to them
phrases.notes: עזרא 2:63

phrases.english: that they should not eat of the most holy things
until a priest stands up with the Urim and Tummim",
say to him:
it is like a person who says to his friend
"until the dead come back to life
and the Messiah, son of David, comes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 7 by heading off an objection from a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That the אורים ותומים lasted until the destruction of the first בית המקדש and never returned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rest of the ברייתא, which reads the פסוק in עזרא 2:63 as speaking about the days of משיח.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק's new explanation of 'early prophets'
steps.stepSummary: Since the אורים ותומים lasted until the first בית המקדש was destroyed, רב נחמן בר יצחק explains 'early prophets' differently. The phrase only comes to exclude the later prophets: חגי, זכריה and מלאכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Who are the 'early prophets'? The phrase comes to leave out חגי, זכריה and מלאכי, because they are the later prophets.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא's answer (דוד, שמואל, שלמה) has been pushed aside, so the גמרא gives a new answer. 'Early prophets' means every prophet before the last three, חגי, זכריה and מלאכי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the old answer is being dropped. Now 'early prophets' covers the whole first בית המקדש period. That fits the ברייתא: the אורים ותומים stopped when the first בית המקדש fell, and they were never used in the time of the later prophets.
steps.whatToRemember: The final answer: 'early prophets' means all the prophets before חגי, זכריה and מלאכי. So the אורים ותומים lasted through the whole first בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Who are "the early prophets"?
It comes to exclude Chaggai, Zecharyah and Malachi,
who are the later prophets.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Because the ברייתא in steps 7-8 shows the אורים ותומים lasted past שלמה, רב הונא's answer is dropped and a new one is given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who are the 'early prophets' in the משנה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All the prophets except the last three, חגי, זכריה and מלאכי, who are called the later prophets.

steps.title: Proof that חגי, זכריה and מלאכי were the last prophets
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that once חגי, זכריה and מלאכי died, רוח הקודש left ישראל. This shows they really were the last group of prophets.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: Once חגי, זכריה and מלאכי died, רוח הקודש left ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רב נחמן בר יצחק. It shows that חגי, זכריה and מלאכי were the very last prophets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק called these three 'the later prophets.' The ברייתא confirms that prophecy ended with them. That gives a clear dividing line between the 'early' and the 'later' prophets.

keyTerms.meaning: as the רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
the Divine Spirit, the spirit of prophecy

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
From when Chaggai, Zecharyah and Malachi died,
the Divine Spirit departed from Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 9's claim that חגי, זכריה and מלאכי are the 'later' prophets.
steps.raayaObject: That חגי, זכריה and מלאכי were the last prophets.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: once they died, רוח הקודש left ישראל.

steps.title: Even after prophecy ended, a heavenly voice was still used
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that even after רוח הקודש left, people still used a בת קול, a voice from Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even so, they still made use of a בת קול.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more point: there was still some message from Heaven, the בת קול. This line sets up the two stories that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Prophecy had ended, but contact with Heaven did not stop completely. A lower level, the בת קול, still existed. The next steps give two examples of it.

keyTerms.meaning: a heavenly voice, a lower level than prophecy

phrases.english: And even so,
they would make use of a heavenly voice,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן הָיוּ מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁים בְּבַת קוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from step 10 and adds what remained after prophecy ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After prophecy stopped, a בת קול was still used.

steps.title: The heavenly voice in יריחו points to הלל הזקן
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן were gathered in Jericho when a בת קול said one person there was fit for the שכינה to rest on him, but his generation was not. They all looked at הלל הזקן. When he died, they praised him as pious, humble, and a student of עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they were sitting at a meal in the upper room of the house of Gurya in Jericho. A בת קול came from Heaven and said: 'There is one person here who deserves to have the שכינה rest on him, but his generation does not deserve it.' They all looked at הלל הזקן. When he died, they eulogized him: 'Alas, pious one! Alas, humble one! Student of עזרא!'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first example of a בת קול being used after prophecy ended. It shows how great הלל הזקן was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story proves the point of step 11: a בת קול really did speak after the last prophets. It also teaches that someone could be personally fit for prophecy and still not receive it, because his generation was not worthy.

keyTerms.meaning: reclining, sitting together at a meal

phrases.english: For once they were reclining at a meal
in the upper room of the house of Gurya in Jericho,

phrases.aramaic: נִתְּנָה עֲלֵיהֶן בַּת קוֹל מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאָמְרָה:
phrases.english: a heavenly voice was given to them from Heaven and said:
There is one person among you
who is fit for the Divine Presence to rest on him,
but his generation is not fit for it.
They set their eyes on Hillel the Elder.
And when he died, they eulogized him:
"Alas, pious one! Alas, humble one!
Student of Ezra!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first story showing that a בת קול was used after prophecy ended.
steps.raayaObject: That a בת קול was still used after prophecy ended.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the בת קול in Jericho that pointed to הלל הזקן.

steps.title: The heavenly voice in יבנה points to שמואל הקטן
steps.stepSummary: Later, in יבנה, the same kind of בת קול spoke again. This time the רבנן looked at שמואל הקטן. When he died, they praised him as humble, pious, and a student of הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time they were sitting in an upper room in יבנה. A בת קול came from Heaven and said to them: 'There is one person here who deserves to have the שכינה rest on him, but his generation does not deserve it.' They all looked at שמואל הקטן. When he died, they eulogized him: 'Alas, humble one! Alas, pious one! Student of הלל!'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second, later example of a בת קול. It is almost word-for-word like the הלל story, but it is about שמואל הקטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repeat shows that the בת קול kept speaking in later generations too. The eulogy calls שמואל הקטן 'a student of הלל,' linking him to the great person of the first story.

keyTerms.meaning: Yavneh, a town that was a center of Torah learning

steps.whatToRemember: Prophecy ended with חגי, זכריה and מלאכי, but a בת קול still spoke. It identified great people like הלל and שמואל הקטן, who were fit for prophecy while their generations were not.

phrases.english: And again, another time, they were reclining
in an upper room in Yavneh,
a heavenly voice was given to them from Heaven,
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'to them' (round brackets). The corrected wording says 'upon them' (square brackets), just like in the הלל story.

phrases.english: and it said to them:
There is one person among you
who is fit for the Divine Presence to rest on him
but his generation is not worthy of it.
They set their eyes on Shmuel HaKatan.
And when he died, they eulogized him:
"Alas, humble one! Alas, pious one!
Student of Hillel!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, later story of the same kind as step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That a בת קול continued to be used in later generations.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the בת קול in יבנה that pointed to שמואל הקטן.

steps.title: שמואל הקטן predicts disaster as he dies
steps.stepSummary: As he was dying, שמואל הקטן predicted that leading רבנן would be killed and great troubles would come to the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as he was dying, he (שמואל הקטן) also said: שמעון and ישמעאל are headed for the sword, their friends for death, the rest of the people for plunder, and many troubles will come upon the nation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more detail about שמואל הקטן: the frightening words he said right before he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 showed that שמואל הקטן was worthy of the שכינה. Here we see a sign of that: as he died, he spoke about the future in a way that sounds almost like prophecy. He foresaw that great leaders would be killed and the nation would suffer.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of his death
For the sword (to be killed by the sword)
For plunder (their property will be robbed)

phrases.english: And he too said at the time of his death:
phrases.notes: "He" is שמואל הקטן from the last story.

phrases.english: Shimon and Yishmael are for the sword,
phrases.notes: He means רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: and their colleagues are for killing,
and the rest of the people are for plunder,

phrases.aramaic: וְעָקָן סַגִּיאִין עֲתִידִין לְמֵיתֵי עַל עַמָּא.
phrases.english: and many troubles are destined to come upon the people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final detail to the story of שמואל הקטן from Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before he died, שמואל הקטן foresaw that the leaders would be killed and the nation would suffer.

steps.title: No eulogy for רבי יהודה בן בבא
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן wanted to praise רבי יהודה בן בבא as pious and humble, but they could not, because people killed by the government are not eulogized.
steps.simpleTranslation: They also wanted to say about רבי יהודה בן בבא, "Alas, the pious one! Alas, the humble one!" But the times were too dangerous, because we do not eulogize people killed by the government.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of one more great person who deserved the same praise as הלל and שמואל הקטן, but did not get it out loud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier stories, the רבנן praised הלל and שמואל הקטן with these same words. They wanted to do the same for רבי יהודה בן בבא. They could not, because the Roman government killed him, and people were not allowed to eulogize those the government had executed.

keyTerms.meaning: Alas, pious one! Alas, humble one! (words of praise in a eulogy)
The moment was thrown into turmoil (the times were too dangerous)

steps.whatToRemember: הלל and שמואל הקטן were marked by a בת קול as fit for the שכינה and were eulogized as 'pious and humble.' The רבנן wanted to give רבי יהודה בן בבא the same praise, but could not, because the government had killed him.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא
phrases.english: And also about Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava
they wanted to say, "Alas, pious one! Alas, humble one!"
but the moment was thrown into turmoil,
because we do not eulogize those killed by the government.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא בִּקְּשׁוּ לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of praised רבנן from Steps 12-13 and closes it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People killed by the government are not eulogized, so רבי יהודה בן בבא did not get the praise he deserved.

steps.title: The שמיר and רבי יהודה's literal reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the שמיר. A ברייתא explains that it was used to build the בית המקדש, and רבי יהודה says the פסוק means exactly what it says.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said the שמיר stopped when the בית המקדש was destroyed. The רבנן taught: the שמיר is what שלמה used to build the בית המקדש, as the פסוק says, "The house, when it was built, was built of whole stone from the quarry." These words mean exactly what they say. This is רבי יהודה's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line in the משנה, about the שמיר, and brings a ברייתא that explains what it was for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the פסוק literally: the stones came to the building site whole, and no iron tool cut them. So the cutting had to be done by the שמיר, a special creature that could split stone without iron. This sets up רבי נחמיה's challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A special tiny creature that could cut through stone
The words mean exactly what is written

phrases.aramaic: מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בָּטַל הַשָּׁמִיר כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: From when the Temple was destroyed, the shamir ceased, etc.
The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁמִיר שֶׁבּוֹ בָּנָה שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: The shamir with which Solomon built the Temple,
as it is said: "And the house, when it was built,
was built of whole stone from the quarry" —
phrases.notes: מלכים א 6:7

phrases.english: the words are as they are written,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, the שמיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the stones of the בית המקדש were cut only by the שמיר, never by iron tools.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: another פסוק says saws were used
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה challenges רבי יהודה with a פסוק that says the stones were cut with saws.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said to him: How can you say that? Doesn't another פסוק say, "All these were costly stones... sawed with saws"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה attacks רבי יהודה's literal reading by pointing to a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stones were cut with saws, then iron tools were used. That seems to contradict רבי יהודה's claim that no iron touched the stones and only the שמיר cut them.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it possible to say so? (a strong challenge)
But hasn't it already been said?

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya said to him:
And is it possible to say so?
But hasn't it already been said:
"All these were costly stones, etc.,
sawed with saws"!
phrases.notes: מלכים א 7:9

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר כֵּן? וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's reading from Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that no iron tools cut the stones
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק says the stones were sawed, and saws are iron tools.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: cut outside, brought inside
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה explains that the פסוק about no tools being heard only means no tools were used inside the building itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the פסוק mean when it says, "was not heard in the house while it was being built"? It means שלמה prepared the stones outside and brought them inside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה gives his own reading of the פסוק רבי יהודה relied on, so both פסוקים fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "not heard in the house" only limit where the tools were used. Iron saws were used outside the בית המקדש area, and the finished stones were carried in. So no iron tool was heard inside, but iron still cut the stones.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the פסוק come to teach?

steps.confusionAlert: רבי נחמיה does not say iron was allowed inside the בית המקדש. He agrees no iron was used there. He only says the stones were cut with iron somewhere else first.

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach when it says:
"was not heard in the house while it was being built"?
phrases.notes: מלכים א 6:7. The full פסוק says no hammer, axe, or iron tool was heard.

phrases.english: That he would prepare the stones outside,
and bring them inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי נחמיה finishes his argument by explaining the פסוק רבי יהודה used.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the פסוק so that it limits only where tools were used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק means no iron tool ever touched the stones.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק means only that no iron tool was used inside the building; the stones were sawed outside.

steps.title: רבי settles: Temple stones and palace stones
steps.stepSummary: רבי says רבי יהודה is right about the stones of the בית המקדש, and רבי נחמיה is right about the stones of שלמה's own palace.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: רבי יהודה's words seem right for the stones of the בית המקדש, and רבי נחמיה's words seem right for the stones of שלמה's house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי makes peace between the two views by saying each one is talking about a different building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about saws (מלכים א 7:9) is really about שלמה's palace, so iron was used there. The פסוק about whole stones is about the בית המקדש, so there only the שמיר was used.

keyTerms.meaning: The stones of the בית המקדש
The stones of his (שלמה's) own house

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, no iron tool ever cut the stones of the בית המקדש, so the שמיר did that work. Saws were used only for שלמה's palace.

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: "רבי" alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.aramaic: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּאַבְנֵי מִקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: The words of Rabbi Yehuda seem correct regarding the Temple stones,
and the words of Rabbi Nechemya regarding the stones of his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The stones of the בית המקדש were cut only by the שמיר; iron saws were used only for שלמה's palace.

steps.title: What was the שמיר for, according to רבי נחמיה?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי נחמיה holds that saws cut the stones, the גמרא asks what the שמיר was needed for.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי נחמיה, what did the שמיר come for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that sets up the next step: if iron cut the stones, what job was left for the שמיר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the שמיר was used to build the בית המקדש. But רבי נחמיה says iron saws cut the stones outside, so the שמיר seems to have no job. The גמרא needs to find one.

keyTerms.meaning: For what did it come? What was it for?

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Nechemya,
for what purpose did the shamir come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבי נחמיה's view by asking what role is left for the שמיר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the שמיר was used for, if iron tools cut the stones of the בית המקדש.

steps.title: The שמיר engraved the stones of the חושן
steps.stepSummary: The שמיר was needed for the stones of the חושן and אפוד, which had to be engraved without ink and without being scratched by a knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed for what a ברייתא teaches: these stones may not be written on with ink, because the פסוק says "engraved like a seal." And they may not be scratched with a knife, because the פסוק says "in their fullness."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the שמיר had a different job: engraving the tribes' names on the precious stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים create a puzzle. "Engraved like a seal" means the names must be cut in, not written in ink. But "in their fullness" means the stones must stay whole, so no knife may scratch away any of the stone. Only the שמיר could make the letters without a tool removing pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for (it is needed for)
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: He needs it for what was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָנִים הַלָּלוּ אֵין כּוֹתְבִין אוֹתָן בִּדְיוֹ,
phrases.english: These stones may not be written on with ink,
phrases.notes: These are the stones of the חושן and אפוד, which had the names of the tribes on them.

phrases.english: because it is said: "engravings of a seal,"
phrases.notes: שמות 28:21

phrases.english: and they may not be scratched with a scalpel,
because it is said: "in their fullness,"
phrases.notes: שמות 28:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי נחמיה, the שמיר was used to engrave the stones of the חושן and אפוד, which could be neither inked nor scratched with a knife.

steps.title: How the שמיר engraved the stones without cutting them
steps.stepSummary: The names were written on the stones in ink, the שמיר was held near them from outside, and the stones split open along the lines by themselves without losing anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he writes on the stones in ink and shows them the שמיר from outside, and they split open by themselves. It is like a fig that splits in the summer without losing anything, and like a valley that cracks in the rainy season without losing anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from the last step by explaining exactly how the שמיר did the engraving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said the stones of the חושן could not be engraved with ink or with a knife. Here we learn that the ink was only a guide line on top, and the שמיר split the stone along that line without touching it. The fig and valley comparisons show that the stone cracked open without any piece being removed.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 21 said 'not with ink,' yet here they do write in ink. The ink was only a guide. The letters were not made of ink; they were made by the stone splitting.

phrases.english: Rather, he writes on them in ink,
phrases.notes: The ink only marks where the letters go. The letters themselves get made by the splitting.

phrases.english: and shows them the שמיר from outside,
and they split open by themselves,
like this fig that splits in the summer days
and is not missing anything,
and like this valley, which cracks in the rainy season,
and is not missing anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 21 by showing how the שמיר was actually used.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Ink marks the letters, and the שמיר held nearby makes the stone split along them without removing any material.

steps.title: A ברייתא describes the שמיר
steps.stepSummary: The שמיר was the size of a barley grain, was created during the six days of creation, and nothing hard could stand up to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: This שמיר is the size of a barley grain. It was created during the six days of creation, and nothing hard can withstand it.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know what the שמיר did, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells us what it was like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives three facts: it was tiny, it was made at the time of creation, and it could break anything hard. That last fact sets up the next question: how could anyone store something that breaks everything?

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught, which introduces a ברייתא

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: This שמיר,
its size is like a barley grain,
and it was created during the six days of creation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין כׇּל דָּבָר קָשֶׁה יָכוֹל לַעֲמוֹד בְּפָנָיו.
phrases.english: and nothing hard can stand up to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how the שמיר was used to what the שמיר was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שמיר was tiny, made at creation, and could break anything hard.

steps.title: How was the שמיר stored?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what the שמיר was kept in, since it could break anything hard.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what do they keep it?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a practical question, setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If nothing hard can withstand the שמיר, then any normal container would break. So we need to know how it was stored safely.

phrases.english: In what do they keep it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the statement that nothing hard can withstand the שמיר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What container could hold the שמיר without being broken.

steps.title: Stored in wool, inside a lead vessel full of bran
steps.stepSummary: They wrapped it in wool and put it in a lead container filled with barley bran.
steps.simpleTranslation: They wrap it in tufts of wool and place it in a lead vessel full of barley bran.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers how the שמיר was stored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soft materials like wool and bran are not 'hard,' so the שמיר does not break them. That is how they could keep it safely.

phrases.english: They wrap it in tufts of wool,
and place it in a vessel of lead
full of barley bran.

steps.whatToRemember: The שמיר engraved the חושן stones by splitting them along ink lines. It was tiny, made at creation, broke anything hard, and was kept wrapped in soft materials.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the storage question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wrapped in wool inside a lead vessel filled with barley bran.

steps.title: רבי אמי: fine silk and white glass stopped after the first בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says that once the first בית המקדש was destroyed, shiny silk and white glass stopped existing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי says: From when the first בית המקדש was destroyed, shiny silk and white glass stopped existing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another teaching about special things that were lost when the first בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds to the theme of the משנה, which lists good things that disappeared over time. רבי אמי adds two fine materials: shiny silk and white glass.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami says:
From when the First Temple was destroyed,
shiny silk stopped existing,
and white glass.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: מִשֶּׁחָרַב מִקְדָּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: more things lost after the destruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shiny silk and white glass stopped after the first בית המקדש was destroyed.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי אמי and adds more items
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same as רבי אמי and adds iron chariots. Some add congealed wine from שניר that looked like round fig cakes.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: From when the first בית המקדש was destroyed, shiny silk, white glass, and iron chariots stopped existing. Some say: even congealed wine that came from שניר, which looked like round cakes of pressed figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי אמי and adds a few more items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats רבי אמי's two items, which supports him. It also adds iron chariots, and a second opinion adds a special thick wine from שניר.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way, which introduces a supporting ברייתא

phrases.english: This is also taught in a ברייתא:
From when the First Temple was destroyed,
shiny silk stopped existing,
and white glass, and iron chariots;
and some say: even congealed wine
that comes from Senir,
phrases.notes: שניר is another name for the חרמון mountain.

phrases.english: which looks like round cakes of pressed figs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אמי's statement with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's list of what stopped after the first בית המקדש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same list, plus iron chariots and congealed wine

steps.title: What is נופת צופים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words נופת צופים and asks what they mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And נופת צופים.' What is נופת צופים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a phrase from the משנה and asks what it means, setting up three answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed נופת צופים among the good things that stopped. The phrase is unclear, so the גמרא asks for a definition.

keyTerms.meaning: A sweet delicacy listed in the משנה; its meaning is discussed here

phrases.english: The משנה said: And נופת צופים.
What is נופת צופים?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to explaining the משנה's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase נופת צופים.

steps.title: רב: fine flour that floats on the sieve
steps.stepSummary: רב says it is the finest flour that floats on top of the sieve and tastes like dough kneaded with honey and oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: Fine flour that floats on top of the sieve, and it tastes like dough kneaded with honey and oil.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first explanation of נופת צופים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads נופת as related to נפה (sieve) and צופים as related to צפה (floats). So it is flour that floats on the sieve and is very sweet.

phrases.english: Rav says:
Fine flour that floats on top of the sieve,
phrases.notes: Hear the wordplay: נפה sounds like נופת, and צפה sounds like צופים.

phrases.english: and it is like dough kneaded with honey and oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: סוֹלֶת שֶׁצָּפָה עַל גַּבֵּי נָפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Fine flour that floats on the sieve and tastes like dough with honey and oil.

steps.title: לוי: two loaves that swell until they touch
steps.stepSummary: לוי says it means two loaves stuck to the oven wall that keep rising until they reach each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי says: Two loaves stuck in the oven that keep swelling until they reach each other.
steps.whatsHappening: לוי gives a second, different explanation of נופת צופים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of flour, לוי says it is a kind of bread. Two loaves baked on the oven wall rise so much that they meet.

phrases.english: And Levi says:
two loaves stuck in the oven
that keep on swelling,
until they reach each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same question as רב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two loaves in the oven that rise until they touch.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: honey from high places
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says נופת צופים is honey that comes from high places.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי says: This is honey that comes from high places.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a third explanation of נופת צופים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads צופים as related to ציפיא, high places. So it is honey brought from the heights.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
This is honey that comes from the high places.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: זֶה דְּבַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question of step 28.

steps.title: Where is this meaning found?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what shows that honey comes from high places.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is this understood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for רבי יהושע בן לוי's explanation, setting up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not obvious that honey is connected to high places. The גמרא wants a source for this idea.

phrases.english: From where is this understood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי יהושע בן לוי's explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that honey comes from high places.

steps.title: רב ששת's תרגום: bees bring honey from mountain plants
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת translated a פסוק to say bees fly over the heights of the world and bring honey from mountain plants.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב ששת translated: 'Like the bees spread out and fly over the heights of the world and bring honey from the plants of the mountain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting רב ששת's Aramaic translation of a פסוק about bees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's translation says bees gather honey from mountain plants. This shows that honey is connected to high places, which supports רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three explanations of נופת צופים: רב says floating fine flour, לוי says two loaves that rise until they touch, and רבי יהושע בן לוי says honey from high places, supported by רב ששת's translation about bees.

phrases.english: As Rav Sheshet translates:
phrases.notes: He is translating 'כאשר תעשינה הדבורים' (דברים 1:44).

phrases.english: Like the bees spread out
and fly over the heights of the world
and bring honey from the plants of the mountain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 32 with a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב ששת's תרגום shows bees bring honey from mountain plants, so honey comes from high places.

steps.title: A משנה about poured liquids mentions 'זיפים' honey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מכשירין: a poured stream does not carry טומאה back up, except for thick 'זיפים' honey and wafer batter.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: anything poured stays טהור, except for זיפים honey and wafer batter.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the previous steps were about honey, the גמרא brings another משנה that mentions a special kind of honey. This sets up the question of what 'זיפים' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, when you pour from a טהור vessel into a טמא one, the stream does not make the top vessel טמא. Thick honey and batter are different, because they hold together like one connected piece. The word 'זיפים' is unclear, so the next step asks about it.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Thin wafer batter, a very thick liquid

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה from מכשירין 5:9.

phrases.english: Anything poured is pure,
phrases.notes: He means the stream doesn't carry טומאה up from the lower vessel to the upper one.

phrases.english: except for zifim honey and wafer batter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the honey of נופת צופים to another משנה that mentions a special honey.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poured stream does not transfer טומאה, except for זיפים honey and wafer batter.

steps.title: What does 'זיפים' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word זיפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'זיפים'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the unusual word 'זיפים' means. Two answers follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple question about a word. It is not a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What is 'zifim'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the משנה just quoted.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: honey good enough to be faked
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says זיפים means honey that people can falsify.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: it is honey that people fake with.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains 'זיפים' as coming from the word for faking or falsifying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The honey is so fine and valuable that people can mix cheaper things into it and nobody notices. רבי יוחנן reads the name as a description of the honey's quality.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
Honey that they falsify with it.
phrases.notes: He means it is so good that people can mix other things in and nobody can tell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זיפים = honey of such quality that it can be faked.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: honey named after the place זיף
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says זיפים is named after a place called זיף, mentioned in יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: it is named after its place, as the פסוק says 'זיף, טלם and בעלות'.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a second answer: 'זיפים' is a place name, not a description.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads the word as describing the honey's quality. ריש לקיש reads it as a place name, and he brings a פסוק to show that a town called זיף exists.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish says:
It is named after its place,
as it is written: 'Ziph and Telem and Bealoth.'
phrases.notes: יהושע 15:24

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second answer, which argues with רבי יוחנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זיפים = honey from the town of זיף.

steps.title: The same word appears in a פסוק about דוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a similar case: the 'זיפים' who told שאול that דוד was hiding among them.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the same way you can say about the פסוק: 'When the זיפים came and told שאול, isn't דוד hiding with us...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a parallel. The same word 'זיפים' shows up in תהלים, and the next steps explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only introduces the פסוק and gives no explanation yet. It prepares the same two-sided disagreement about a different use of the word.

phrases.english: Similarly, you say:
'When the zifim came and said to Saul,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 54:2

phrases.english: 'Is not David...' etc.
phrases.notes: The פסוק goes on: 'hiding himself with us'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same word question to a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the פסוק about the זיפים as a parallel case.

steps.title: Who were the זיפים in the פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'זיפים' means in the פסוק about דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'זיפים'?
steps.whatsHappening: The same question is asked again, this time about the people in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא repeats the question on purpose, because the word now describes people and not honey.

phrases.english: What is 'zifim'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the פסוק just quoted.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: people who twisted their words
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the זיפים were people who falsified their words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: people who falsify their words.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן stays consistent with his earlier view. 'זיפים' comes from the word for faking, so these were deceitful people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the honey could be faked, these people faked their words. They informed on דוד to שאול.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
People who falsify their words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer, matching רבי יוחנן's view about the honey.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: named after their town
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the זיפים were named after their town, זיף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: named after their place, as it says 'זיף, טלם and בעלות'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the place-name explanation, the same approach ריש לקיש took about the honey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the second opinion is said by רבי אלעזר rather than ריש לקיש, but the reasoning is the same. 'זיפים' simply means people from זיף.
steps.whatToRemember: In both places, one view reads 'זיפים' as 'faking' (רבי יוחנן) and the other reads it as the town זיף.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar says:
It is named after their place,
as it is written: 'Ziph and Telem and Bealoth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second answer, which disagrees with רבי יוחנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זיפים = people from the town of זיף.

steps.title: Who are the 'people of faith' who ceased?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'אנשי אמנה ceased', and רבי יצחק explains these are people who trust in הקב"ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And people of faith ceased.' רבי יצחק says: these are people who believe in הקב"ה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to our משנה and explains the next item on its list, 'אנשי אמנה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק defines 'אמנה' as faith and trust in הקב"ה. The next step brings a ברייתא to support this.

phrases.english: And people of faith ceased.
Rabbi Yitzchak says:
These are people
who believe in the Holy One, Blessed be He.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the זיפים side topic to the list in our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אנשי אמנה are people with complete trust in הקב"ה.

steps.title: Bread today, worry about tomorrow
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי אליעזר הגדול says someone who has bread today but worries about tomorrow has little faith.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי אליעזר הגדול says, anyone who has bread in his basket and says 'what will I eat tomorrow?' is one of those with little faith.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבי יצחק, showing that 'אמנה' is about trusting הקב"ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same word, 'קטני אמנה', for someone who doesn't trust הקב"ה to provide. This shows that 'אמנה' means faith in הקב"ה, just as רבי יצחק said.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Bread in his basket (food for today)

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ פַּת בְּסַלּוֹ
phrases.english: Anyone who has bread in his basket
and says 'What will I eat tomorrow?'
is nothing but one of those of little faith.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יצחק's definition.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's reading of אנשי אמנה as trust in הקב"ה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי אליעזר הגדול about worrying over tomorrow's bread.

steps.title: Small faith costs even צדיקים their reward
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads 'כי מי בז ליום קטנות' to mean that צדיקים lose part of their future reward because of their small faith.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי אלעזר meant: what does 'who scorned the day of small things' mean? What caused the צדיקים's table in the future to be plundered? The smallness in them, that they did not fully trust הקב"ה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the idea of little faith to a teaching of רבי אלעזר about a פסוק in זכריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר splits the words: 'בז' as plundering and 'קטנות' as smallness of faith. Even צדיקים can lose part of their reward in the future world (their 'table') when their trust in הקב"ה is not complete. This adds weight to how serious the קטני אמנה idea is.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Table' here does not mean real furniture. It stands for the reward of the צדיקים in the future.

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״כִּי מִי בַז לְיוֹם קְטַנּוֹת״ —
phrases.english: What is meant by 'For who has scorned the day of small things'?
phrases.notes: זכריה 4:10

phrases.english: What caused the righteous
to have their table plundered in the future?
The smallness that was in them,
that they did not believe in the Holy One, Blessed be He.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the idea of small faith matches רבי אלעזר's reading of a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lack of complete trust in הקב"ה causes even צדיקים to lose part of their future reward.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that faith in הקב"ה is not a small matter. Even righteous people are held to account for it.

steps.title: רבא's different reading: the small children of the wicked
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins another reading of the same פסוק: 'קטנות' refers to the young children of wicked Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: these are the small children of the wicked of ישראל...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a different explanation of 'יום קטנות'. His statement continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'smallness of faith', רבא reads 'קטנות' as literally small children, the children of רשעים. What he says about them comes on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: The young children of the wicked of ישראל

phrases.english: Rava says:
These are the small children of the wicked of Israel,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same פסוק that רבי אלעזר explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'יום קטנות' refers to the young children of wicked Jews (continued on the next עמוד).
